BiblicalUsage: Rabshakeh was an Assyrian official — a title, 'chief cupbearer,' carried as a name. Sennacherib sent him from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem, and he stood by the conduit of the upper pool and cried with a loud voice in the Jews' language, mocking the God of Israel and offering surrender.
TheologicalSignificance: This tells me that Rabshakeh's loud voice is the enemy's oldest tactic: to make God's people doubt Him in their own language, where everyone can hear.
RelatedPeople: King Hezekiah; Sennacherib, King of Assyria
